name: macropad
title: Macropad for the thin module
orientation: A circuit board, made by a fab (JLCPCB), not printed. Seen from above: twelve keys in three columns and four rows, a DO-35 diode in the gaps beside each; the module's USB-C on the top edge. Front: the module above the keys, display sockets at its ends. Rear: the module under the top row, parts facing down.

mount.rule: front: the module on top, beyond the keys, with display sockets at its ends; rear: the module under the top row of keys, on pin headers, the board no bigger than the keys and the module
mount.label: Module

cols.rule: Columns of keys: three, the module's end columns being three key widths apart
cols.label: Columns

module_gap.rule: Front: the module's bottom edge this far beyond the top row of keys' square

castle_out.rule: Front: each pin's pad reaches this far beyond the module's edge, for the solder fillet on a castellated half hole

label_gap.rule: Silkscreen labels this far from the pads they name

display_scl.rule: SPI display: SCL (clock), the module's display column

via_hole.rule: The router's vias: a 0.3 mm hole, JLCPCB's standard (no extra charge), with the ring it recommends

socket_turn.rule: The display sockets turned so pin 1 (GND) is at the bottom of the column, as in the module's own display column

label_char.rule: Silkscreen: a character's width, as a share of its height (tscircuit's font)

track.rule: Signal track width: well over JLCPCB's least on a cheap two-layer board

clearance.rule: Copper to copper, kept by the router

row_gpio.rule: The rows' GPIO (each row's diodes' cathodes), along the module's bottom row: 26 to 29, beside the columns'

col_gpio.rule: The columns' GPIO (each column's switches' pin 1): 20 to 22. GPIO 0 and 1 (UART), 2 and 3 (I2C display) and the SPI display's pins stay free

diode_turn.rule: Each diode turned to lie along its gap between two columns of switches, its cathode down

socket_gap.rule: Front: each display socket's pins this far beyond the module's pads

socket_height.rule: A standard 0.1 in female socket's height
socket_height.source: KiCad footprint library, Connector_PinSocket_2.54mm (8.5 mm sockets)

edge_keep.rule: Front: the board's edge this far beyond the module's pads and the sockets' pads (over JLCPCB's 0.3 mm copper to edge)

mount_rows.rule: Mounting holes where four keys meet, below these rows (0 the top row), either side of the middle column: in the gaps, under the keycaps' corners (each hole sized by the board's mount(), from its thread's set)

finish.rule: 1: tracks finished for the fab once routed (square pad exits, acute corners filled); 0 to compare without

display_stack.rule: Front: the SPI display's socket, two standard sockets stacked (17 mm): the display reaches over the top row of keys, and this lifts its board clear of the DSA keycaps (the assembly checks the gap)
